en: Many think Jose Rizal was the first president, but Emilio Aguinaldo actually held that title as the first president of the Philippines.
Contrary to popular belief, the Philippines has over 100 distinct regional languages, even though Filipino is the sole national language.
The eight rays on the Philippine flag's sun actually represent the first eight provinces that revolted against Spain, not eight geographic regions.
Many think America granted Philippine independence, but June 12 actually commemorates Emilio Aguinaldo's 1898 declaration of independence from Spain.
The Philippine legislative branch is not just the Senate, but a bicameral Congress consisting of both the Senate and the House of Representatives.
People often mistake the bald eagle for our national bird, but the critically endangered Philippine eagle holds that official title.
While Jose Rizal inspired the movement, Andres Bonifacio actually founded the secret Katipunan society to launch the armed revolution against Spain.
Although often rounded to three centuries, Spanish colonial rule in the Philippines actually lasted for exactly 333 years, from 1565 to 1898.
Many assume the traditional barong tagalog is made of thick fabric, but it is actually crafted from delicate, breathable pineapple fiber to suit the tropical climate.
Many assume the rose is our national flower due to its popularity, but the native sampaguita, a type of jasmine, is the official symbol.
Some believe Filipinos cannot invent modern technology, but Dr. Gregorio Zara actually co-invented the two-way videophone long before modern video calls.
Many think the ancient Baybayin script is a standard alphabet, but it is actually a syllabary where each consonant symbol includes an inherent vowel sound.
